author: Zeno Ren
writer_termination_note: 143 = SIGTERM; the preStop hook drained before the writer stopped
probe_model_choice: databricks-claude-opus-5 rather than opus-5-5, which is intermittently capacity-limited upstream and caused the 2026-10-10 rollback when used as a mandatory gate
independent_sample_method: issued from inside the pod against the public URL, so the client key never left the cluster

schema.no_migration_required: a new table rather than a column on model_provider_preference, which already existed in production; widening that one would have been a real ALTER

build.controller_rebuild_not_needed: operations/ and the APP_FILES set are unchanged in this release

preflight_prerequisites_rechecked.why: the 2026-10-14 first-attempt 403 was a template reference missing from the Role; this release adds no reference, and the Role was re-verified before planning

configmap_change_note: none in this release, so the release-first/apply-after ordering question did not arise

carried_over_from_the_previous_release.item: the four Copilot accounts added to the ConfigMap on 2026-10-14 were waiting for a rolling restart to become visible
carried_over_from_the_previous_release.evidence: 5 Copilot endpoints loaded; the four report [INERT (enabled: false in config)] and appear in /admin/copilot/accounts with enabled=false
carried_over_from_the_previous_release.still_required_to_serve_traffic: discover -> select models -> enable, then one further restart

routing_behaviour_note: no rule is configured (model_accounts=0, model_preferences=0), so every model keeps the default order and all enabled accounts

contract_change.what: the Dashboard keys panel holds the LB API Key in page memory while unlocked, rather than for a single request
contract_change.why: the panel has four sections and every write needs the key, so the one-request contract meant retyping it per save
unchanged_boundaries: locking clears the rendered identity material
contract_change.upstream_credential_field_excluded: credSecret keeps the one-request contract; holding the LB key is a convenience, that one is a secret

defects_found_while_verifying_and_fixed_: /v1/models asked account_allows directly instead of going through CopilotEndpoint.supports(), so the catalogue advertised a model whose only selected accounts cannot serve it. Found end-to-end, not by unit tests; both the capability path and the wildcard fallback now have regressions.
A failed unlock kept the previously held key, so the panel reported an invalid key while still authorising writes with the key the operator came to replace.
'Not configured' and 'storage is down' are both HTTP 503, so every deployment without credential storage saw a warning on each unlock. fetchJSON now carries the server error code.
operator_errors_this_run: polled `status --directory` for three minutes; the subcommand takes --release-id, so those polls were argument errors rather than status reads. The in-cluster state machine was unaffected.
guessed CredentialStore's constructor and MySQL env var names in the image self-check; corrected against the source before relying on either.
outstanding: Freezing the routing decision at request admission is still not implemented. Within one request `select_endpoint(pinned=…)` holds the account and session affinity holds it across requests, but 'policy changed mid-request' is still covered by pinned rather than structurally. The per-model account layer adds one more mutable dimension, bounded by one retry landing elsewhere.

Azure Foundry credentials still return 401 on every path and have served zero requests. The credentials themselves need replacing; POST /admin/credentials/azure_openai/{account}/validate can confirm once they are.
The four Copilot accounts are loaded and visible but inert. Enabling each needs discover -> select models -> enable, then one further restart.
Copilot price refresh logged a ValueError and retained the previous prices. Pre-existing fail-safe behaviour, not introduced here, and not investigated in this release.
